question: Should OpenClaw intentionally require injected outbound-media readers to provide explicit local roots while accepting the additive public SDK surface used to centralize WhatsApp media behavior?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but only an owner can approve the upgrade-visible reader contract and permanent third-party Plugin SDK surface; the current dirty merge also means that approval must apply to a rebased head.

options.title: Rebase and approve the contract
options.body: Resolve the current merge against main, retain the explicit-root requirement and focused additive SDK APIs, then rerun the affected proof before landing.

options.title: Preserve reader compatibility
options.body: Keep the canonical migration but add a narrowly documented compatibility path for existing injected readers, with tests and an explicit removal or migration plan.

options.title: Narrow the public SDK surface
options.body: Keep WhatsApp on shared internals while revising or reducing the newly exported API until owners agree on the permanent plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Rebase and approve the contract
recommendation.body: Resolve the current merge against main, retain the explicit-root requirement and focused additive SDK APIs, then rerun the affected proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant current-main history shows ownership of the shared outbound-access plumbing and Plugin SDK boundary affected by the compatibility decision.
